import pytest

from f112 import reverse_delete


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "s, c, expected_string, expected_palindrome",
    [
        # Characters removed, remaining string is NOT a palindrome
        ("abcde", "ae", "bcd", False),
        ("abcdef", "b", "acdef", False),
        # Characters removed, remaining string IS a palindrome
        ("abcdedcba", "ab", "cdedc", True),
        ("aabbaa", "ab", "", True),          # everything removed -> empty is palindrome
        ("aba", "xyz", "aba", True),         # nothing removed, already palindrome
        ("", "abc", "", True),               # empty input stays empty
        ("x", "y", "x", True),               # single character is a palindrome
        ("hello", "l", "heo", False),        # repeated chars in c all removed
    ],
)
def test_reverse_delete(s, c, expected_string, expected_palindrome):
    result = reverse_delete(s, c)

    # Postcondition: result is a (string, bool) tuple
    assert isinstance(result, tuple)
    assert len(result) == 2
    assert isinstance(result[0], str)
    assert isinstance(result[1], bool)

    filtered, is_palindrome = result

    # Line 3: every char of s not in c survives, in original order
    expected_filtered = "".join(char for char in s if char not in c)
    assert filtered == expected_string == expected_filtered
    assert all(char not in c for char in filtered)

    # Line 4: second element reports whether filtered string reads the same backwards
    assert is_palindrome == expected_palindrome
    assert is_palindrome == (filtered == filtered[::-1])
